findings.headline: Warsh Jackson Hole aftermath — Kalshi September hike odds at 47%, CME at 55.7%, three FOMC dissenters wanted hike in July
findings.source: Kalshi / CNBC / TheStreet / Axios / Fortune / WSLS / Yahoo Finance / TradingEconomics
findings.summary: Post-Jackson Hole analysis: Kalshi's September rate hike market surged 17 points to 47% after Warsh's speech. CME FedWatch at 55.7% (up ~20pp). Warsh said 'underlying trends have not meaningfully improved' and 'we have work to do' if inflation doesn't ease. Three FOMC members (Hammack, Logan, Kashkari) dissented at July meeting, preferring 25bp hike. Kansas City Fed's Schmid also suggested rates should be higher. Axios: Warsh 'mapped quite clearly into a need for a tighter policy stance' but stopped short of locking in a September hike. Fortune: next CPI data due Sept. 11, just days before Sept. 15-16 FOMC meeting. Heather Long (Navy Federal): 'Warsh opened the door to a Fed rate hike. A hike probably won't come in September, but it will by October or December.' Harvard's Rogoff: Warsh 'showed courage' defying political pressure. KTAR: longer-term rates barely rose, suggesting investors reassured Fed will bring down inflation over time. TradingEconomics: three dissenters 'leaves the door open to a rate increase in September.'

findings.headline: Bessent bond buyback doubling to $4B per operation starting Sep 9 — Guardian calls him 'inept, incompetent, craven,' Raw Story 'worst treasury secretary in history'
findings.source: Yahoo Finance / Guardian / Raw Story / Crooks and Liars / Crypto Briefing / AAS Economics / CNBC
findings.summary: Treasury Secretary Bessent announced doubling buybacks from $2B to $4B per operation for 10-30 year Treasuries, starting September 9. 30Y yield hit 19-year high of 5.33%, eased to ~5.16%. Guardian headline: 'Inept, incompetent, craven: Scott Bessent struggles to clean up the president's mess.' Raw Story: 'worst treasury secretary in history.' Crypto Briefing: plan 'keeps running into the bond market's brick wall.' AAS Economics: 'new bond market crisis?' Whatfinger: Bessent's policy 'not going to work.' Trump distanced himself from Bessent — said he 'acted on his own authority.' Nikkei Asia: ex-official calls intervention 'puzzling.' Boockvar: 'Market is in the driver's seat.' Foreign demand collapsing: China -$60B since February, Dutch pension ABP cut 84%. Fed holdings rose $337B (QT ended, reinvesting). $40T total US debt, $32T in market (100% GDP). Inflation 3.4%.

findings.headline: Iran's Khamenei urges Gulf rulers to identify 'real enemy' — first public message since father killed in February strikes
findings.source: CBS News / Times of India
findings.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei published a written message Sunday on Telegram marking Prophet Muhammad's birthday, urging Gulf leaders to identify their 'real enemy' and calling for Muslim unity and mutual defense. Khamenei has not been seen in public since US-Israeli strikes in February that killed his father, previous Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. He is believed to have been injured. Message coincides with Bessent's G20 push to isolate Iran economically. Iran's FM Araghchi: 'Putting diplomacy back on track isn't impossible. It hinges on U.S. understanding: pressure doesn't work.' Trump: 'not looking to meet' with Iran.

findings.headline: Bessent takes Iran isolation pitch to G20 — Asheville meeting Aug 31-Sep 1, faces resistance from China, India, Russia, Turkey
findings.source: The National / Eurasia Review / Iran Monitor / WSPA / Fox8 / 933 The Drive
findings.summary: Treasury Secretary Bessent hosting G20 finance ministers and central bank governors in Asheville, NC, Aug 31-Sep 1. Will press allies to join 'Operation Economic Outcast' to isolate Iran economically. Senior Treasury official: 'I expect that this will come up in every single bilateral meeting.' Iran Monitor: push faces 'immediate resistance from key Iranian trading partners' including China, India, Russia, Turkey. Rachel Ziemka (Ziemba Insights): 'highly unlikely that the G20 as a group is going to endorse this effort.' China takes ~90% of Iran's crude oil exports. US sanctioned Hong Kong and China-based companies but spared major Chinese banks ahead of Xi-Trump summit next month. China's FM: 'will take all necessary measures.' UAE suspended trade and financial transactions with Iran after missile strikes. Gulf states pouring billions into pipelines to bypass Hormuz. Bessent also targeting Banque Misr (Egypt's second-largest bank) in UAE. Banque Misr action takes effect after month-long public comment period.

findings.headline: Hezbollah rejects all negotiations — US Embassy Beirut: 'taking orders from Iran,' refuses to talk to Lebanese state, US, or Israel
findings.source: CBS News / Economic Times / Asharq Al-Awsat / Emra News
findings.summary: Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem again rejected the Israel-Lebanon framework agreement. US Embassy Beirut stated Saturday on X: 'Hizballah so far does not want to talk to the Lebanese state, nor talk to us, nor talk to Israel, because it is simply taking orders from Iran.' Hezbollah has not been party to any negotiations. Qassem: 'We will keep our heads high and we will not surrender.' Israel operating in self-declared 6-mile 'security zone' inside Lebanon. Regular Israeli strikes, artillery shelling, demolition of civilian buildings continue. Lebanon: 4,300+ killed. Iran's Rezaei threatened intervention if Beirut or southern suburbs targeted. Asharq Al-Awsat: Israel pulled some troops back in 'good faith gesture' toward Lebanon's government. Israel seeking 'new rules of engagement' with Hezbollah.

findings.headline: Trump oil and gas stock trades continued during Iran war — Sen. Warren: 'most corrupt president ever,' Sanders calls war 'endless'
findings.source: CBS News / Sen. Warren / Sen. Sanders / Joint Economic Committee
findings.summary: CBS News: President Trump's investment accounts continued to purchase and sell oil and gas stocks while overseeing the Iran war, per financial disclosure filings through Q2 2026. Holdings jumped from $13-46M range to $17-61M by mid-August. ~3,600 stock/securities trades in first 3 months worth $212M-$695M. Sen. Warren at rally: 'He is the most corrupt president ever in American history... When Donald Trump starts a war with Iran and his oil buddies start making profits like crazy, our job is to call it out.' ExxonMobil Q2 profits: $14B (double YoY). Chevron Q2: $12.1B (quadrupled YoY). Sen. Sanders: 'We've been in a war now for some five-plus months... That war is going to cost us hundreds and hundreds of billions of dollars.' White House: Trump not involved in his trades.

findings.headline: ATF 'major incident' from Qilin ransomware — criminal investigation files breached, DOJ investigating
findings.source: SecurityWeek / Ermer and Suter / Cybernews / ATF confirmation
findings.summary: Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) confirmed cyber incident after Qilin ransomware group claimed attack August 26. ATF declared 'major incident.' Qilin operates ransomware-as-a-service from Russia. Standalone system holding criminal investigation data breached. DOJ investigating with ATF. No evidence or sample of stolen data provided by Qilin. CISA added CVE-2026-53362 to KEV catalog. Pattern of escalating cyber incidents targeting US government agencies continues.

findings.headline: McKesson cyberattack discovered Aug 25 — SEC 8-K filed, healthcare distribution disrupted alongside Boston Scientific
findings.source: Ermer and Suter / CyberInsider / McKesson 8-K filing
findings.summary: NEW FINDING. McKesson, one of the largest healthcare distribution and pharmaceutical companies in the US, discovered a cybersecurity incident on August 25, 2026. SEC 8-K filed. Investigation in early stages. CyberInsider first reported the breach. This is a second major healthcare supply chain cyberattack alongside Boston Scientific (also Aug 25). McKesson distributes pharmaceuticals, medical supplies, and health care information technologies. Combined impact: two major healthcare infrastructure companies hit simultaneously — device shipments (Boston Scientific) and pharmaceutical distribution (McKesson). Hospital supply chains facing dual cyber disruption.

findings.headline: Boston Scientific cyberattack — global disruption continues, implanted device monitoring still available but shipping halted
findings.source: TechJournal / Security Arsenal / MalwareTips / FortaRisks / TechNadu
findings.summary: Boston Scientific August 27 update: function of implanted cardiac rhythm-management devices and existing remote monitoring remain available — most important distinction for patients with active monitoring. However, order-processing and shipping systems still down. No specific CVE, threat actor attribution, or confirmed ransomware family identified. $20.1B annual revenue, 127 countries, 59,000 employees. SEC 8-K filed August 26. Security Arsenal: 'When a company of Boston Scientific's scale discloses that IT operations are impacted, security teams at peer organizations, suppliers, hospitals, and downstream healthcare delivery organizations should treat this as an early warning.' FortaRisks: cyberattack targets operations, not just data. Up to 3-week disruption estimated (Piper Sandler).

findings.headline: Berlin government cyberattack — Rhysida ransomware targets state administration ahead of vote, extortion attempt confirmed
findings.source: InfoSec Today / DeXpose / Boston Institute of Analytics
findings.summary: NEW FINDING. Berlin's state government confirmed extortion attempt following August cyberattack on the city-state's administrative network. Ransomware group Rhysida claimed responsibility on its leak site. Officials refused requested ransom. Attack ahead of important vote. Adds to pattern of escalating government cyberattacks: ATF (Qilin), Berlin government (Rhysida), plus multiple ransomware attacks on US companies (Akira/Gill Rock Drill, TheGentlemen/Party Rental and Chilean energy firm Espinos, Dragonforce/Hogan Omidi). Boston Institute of Analytics: 'From 22 to 28 August 2026, multiple incidents showed a clear pattern' of AI attacks, data breaches, and zero-day threats.

findings.headline: UK airports cyberattack — 8.7 million customer records accessed (Manchester, Stansted, East Midlands)
findings.source: Telegraph / RTE / Independent / Cybernews / SecurityWeek (carried forward)
findings.summary: Manchester Airports Group (MAG) cyber intrusion discovered earlier this week. Data of ~8.7 million customers accessed: car park, lounge, fast track bookings, in-airport wifi sign-ups. Passenger safety unaffected. No threat actor claimed responsibility. Significant UK transportation infrastructure vulnerability exposed. Comes amid elevated CISA advisory posture and escalating global cyberattack pattern.

findings.headline: ECB expected to hike to 2.50% in September — Eurozone inflation forecast 3.3%, France 2.7%, Spain 4.5%, energy-driven

findings.summary: NEW FINDING. Eurozone inflation expected to accelerate to 3.3% in August (preliminary data Sept 1) — highest in three years. France inflation rose to 2.7% from 2.4%. Spain jumped to 4.5% from 3.9%. Energy remains primary driver — Iran war/Hormuz disruption pushing oil, gas, refined products higher. July energy inflation +10% annual. Services inflation 3.3%. Core inflation ~2.5%. MeteoFinanza: ECB 'ample orientation' toward September hike, 25bp to 2.50% deposit rate. ECB July minutes: several Council members saw further hike as probable to prevent energy shock from creating second-round effects. Q2 Eurozone GDP grew 0.4% (double forecasts), reducing recession fears. House of Commons Library: ECB cut rates 8 times June 2024-June 2025, then held until June 2026. Now shifting back to hiking. France Q2 economy stalled, deficit 5.1% GDP (well above 3% EU limit). Global synchronized tightening: Fed hawkish, ECB hiking, BOJ hiking. No major central bank cutting.

Second-hand home prices down ~25% from 2020 in inland cities. Q2 GDP 4.3% (slowest in 3+ years). Trade surplus more than doubled since 2019. 'China Shock 2.0' export fears escalating. Xi redirecting bank credit from real estate to tech but emerging sectors too small to offset housing drag. 'The problem is systemic.' Vanke seeking to extend bond repayments.

Eurasia Review: 4 key issues shaping what's next in Iran war — G20 meeting will be critical test of US economic warfare strategy. European central bankers caught between US pressure on Iran sanctions and domestic energy/inflation crisis from Hormuz closure.

findings.headline: Global port congestion at records — Asian ports, Rhine low water, Panama reducing capacity Sep 3 and Sep 15
findings.source: Drewry / Supply Chain Italy / Linerlytica (carried forward, confirmed)

Suez Canal: some carriers cautiously resuming transits following improved security assessments. Supply Chain Italy: terminals at 90% utilization take ~1 week to recover from 1-day disruption; 75% utilization recovers in 2 days. Industry optimized to reduce unused capacity — little buffer. Hormuz + Panama + Suez + Rhine disruptions compounding with no slack. Panama Canal Authority reducing daily transits further Sep 3, another reduction Sep 15. Storm and hurricane risk flagged for fall.

findings.headline: Gulf states building billions in pipelines to bypass Hormuz — France's Macron and Saudi Crown Prince to discuss oil pipelines

findings.summary: Gulf states pouring billions into building new pipelines to bypass Strait of Hormuz and deliver energy supplies to global markets. France's Macron and Saudi Crown Prince to discuss oil pipeline projects. UAE suspended trade and financial transactions with Iran. Structural adaptation to Hormuz closure accelerating — but pipelines take years to complete. Until then, Hormuz remains critical chokepoint with 4% capacity.

Two exemptions: startup (up to $5M over 4 years) and fundraising (up to $75M in 12-month periods). Safe harbor for transition. Yahoo Finance: 'a future commission can withdraw that entire scheme with a memo.' Paul Hastings: Treasury proposed rulemaking for GENIUS Act implementation (Section 3). White House hosted crypto meeting urging Senate to pass CLARITY Act. FASB proposed treating qualifying stablecoins as cash equivalents Aug 18. Crypto.news: SEC, FASB, and OCC writing crypto rules through rulemaking instead of legislation.

findings.headline: CLARITY Act lost legislative window — Polymarket odds 82% to 16%, Galaxy at 10%, passage likely slips to 2027
findings.source: Tech Insider / Crypto News / Galaxy Digital / OneDayAdvisor / Medium / Crypto.news
findings.summary: CLARITY Act passed House but Senate process incomplete. Senate filed cloture August 8, no final floor vote. Missed August 10 recess deadline. Passage likely slips to 2027. SEC, FASB, OCC writing rules through rulemaking instead. Regulatory uncertainty persists through Congressional inaction.

Stablecoin market peaked at $322.1B in mid-May, now declining as yield-seeking capital exits. Medium: 'where does everything that is not a payment stablecoin live? The CLARITY Act was meant to sort tokens between SEC and CFTC. The Senate draft has not moved.' Full GENIUS Act effect expected by early 2027. Missed statutory deadline by 4 months.

findings.headline: Bitcoin at ~$78,145 — pulled back from $80K, profit-taking near $82K resistance, ETF flows moderating
findings.source: CoinGecko / CoinStats / CoinDesk / Coinbase / Yahoo Finance
findings.summary: CoinGecko: BTC at $78,144.99 with 24h volume of $17.2B. CoinStats: Bitcoin near $77,472 on Aug 28 following 3.7% decline, derivatives data showed reading near $80,338 at earlier point. Coinbase: BTC down 27.75% over past year. ETF flows: 9-day streak hit $3B but momentum moderating. TradingKey: 'pulled back due to profit-taking near $80,000-$82,000 resistance zone. Leverage unwinding and moderated ETF flows reinforced intraday decline.' Risks: Aug 28 options expiry, macro surprises from Jackson Hole, profit-taking $80.5K-$82K, ETF demand may slow. Coinbase: 'Bitcoin outperforming stocks and correlating with gold just when it matters most.' Dormant wallet activity at lowest since 2022 — 2026 on pace for under half of last year's total. Correlation with gold suggests market pricing in monetary dysfunction.

findings.headline: Bessent buybacks start Sep 9 at $4B — 30Y at 19-year high (5.33% peak, ~5.16% current), intervention failing, foreign demand collapsing
findings.source: Yahoo Finance / Guardian / Crypto Briefing / AAS Economics / NBC News / GoldBroker / Raw Story / Crooks and Liars
findings.summary: Treasury buyback operations begin Sep 9 at $4B per operation (doubled from $2B). 30Y yield peaked at 5.33% (19-year high), eased to ~5.16%. NBC News: prior buyback 'did not work' — yields briefly plunged then rose within a day. Guardian: 'inept, incompetent, craven.' Raw Story: 'worst treasury secretary in history.' Crooks and Liars: 30Y at '19-year high.' Crypto Briefing: plan 'keeps running into the bond market's brick wall.' AAS Economics: 'new bond market crisis?' Foreign demand collapsing: China -$60B since February, ABP -84%. Fed holdings rose $337B (QT ended). Fed holds >50% of certain 10-15Y maturities. $40T total debt, $32T market (100% GDP). Three forces: huge issuance, inflation anxiety (3.4%), attractive alternatives. Warsh and Bessent 'at odds.'

findings.headline: China property crisis 6th year — new credit support measures, 'problem is systemic,' Q2 GDP 4.3% slowest in 3+ years
findings.source: Bloomberg / Business Times / Taipei Times / Wikipedia
findings.summary: Bloomberg/Business Times: China unveiled measures to boost financing support for homebuyers and developers. Evergrande founder Xu Jiayin jailed for life. Property sector 6th year of collapse. Millions of partially built properties derelict. Second-hand home prices down ~25% from 2020 in inland cities. Q2 GDP 4.3% (slowest in 3+ years). Trade surplus more than doubled since 2019. 'China Shock 2.0.' Xi redirecting credit from property to tech but emerging sectors too small. 'The problem is systemic.' Vanke seeking to extend bond repayments. Wikipedia: Forbes estimated China's economy dealing with range of challenges due to property crisis. Labor force shrinking due to aging population.

findings.headline: Japan yen carry trade risk ACTIVE — BOJ September hike 84-85%, Warsh hawkish simultaneously, DUAL TIGHTENING threat
findings.source: FXStreet / ActionForex / Japan Times / CNBC / Commerzbank / Investing.com (carried forward, confirmed)
findings.summary: BOJ September hike case maintained: Tokyo core CPI 1.8%, core-core 2.0% (BOJ target). Markets pricing 84-85%. Warsh hawkish simultaneously — US September hike odds at 47-55.7%. BOTH central banks may tighten in September. Japan 10Y JGB at 3% (highest since 1996), 30Y above 4%. US 30Y above 5.16%. Bessent buybacks failing — US yields stay elevated. Investing.com: 'The End of Cheap Yen Could Mean Higher Yields for US Treasury.' If both Fed and BOJ hike in September, spread compresses from both sides — exactly the August 2024 crash mechanism at larger scale. Carry trade unwind risk now ACTIVE. KEY UPCOMING: BOJ September meeting (expected hike), Fed Sept 15-16 FOMC, CPI Sept 11.

findings.headline: Eurozone inflation heading to 3.3% — ECB expected to hike to 2.50% in September, France 2.7%, Spain 4.5%, energy-driven
findings.source: MeteoFinanza / Kleine Zeitung / EcoIran / Sudan Independent
findings.summary: NEW FINDING. Eurozone inflation expected to accelerate to 3.3% in August (preliminary Sept 1) — highest in three years. France 2.7% (up from 2.4%), Spain 4.5% (up from 3.9%). Energy primary driver — Iran war/Hormuz pushing oil, gas, refined products higher. July energy inflation +10% annual. Services 3.3%. Core ~2.5%. ECB expected to hike 25bp to 2.50% deposit rate at Sept 9-10 meeting. ECB July minutes: several Council members saw further hike as probable. Q2 Eurozone GDP grew 0.4% (double forecasts). France Q2 economy stalled, deficit 5.1% GDP. Global synchronized tightening: Fed + ECB + BOJ all potentially hiking in September. UNPRECEDENTED triple-tightening.

findings.headline: Oil prices weekly plunge 4%+ — Brent $88.29 Friday close, demand destruction fears from Fed tightening vs Hormuz supply disruption
findings.source: Blockonomi / Athens Times / Economic Times / Straits.live / ECIKS
findings.summary: NEW FINDING. Brent settled at $88.29 Friday, down 5%+ on week. ECIKS: oil hit $90.55 on Aug 28 before retreating. Weekly plunge driven by Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech (demand destruction fears) + rumors of Hormuz deal talks advancing. But Straits.live: Hormuz still at 4% capacity, 3 transits vs 85/day normal. Tension between demand-side tightening (Fed hikes) and supply-side disruption (Hormuz closure). Blockonomi: 'Fed tightening and Hormuz negotiations intensify.' If Hormuz talks fail AND Fed hikes, oil could spike back above $90 while financial conditions tighten — stagflationary scenario. If Hormuz talks succeed, oil could drop sharply, easing inflation pressure.
